clips.title: The story
paras: Across Mulgore, Arra'chea roams while Cairne Bloodhoof calls young hunters to prove their worth. The kodo's horn confirms a hunter can track prey and provide for the Shu'halo.

Passing the Rites of the Earthmother earns a youth a place atop Thunder Bluff, but High Chieftain Cairne Bloodhoof still expects his people to prove their worth. For the tauren, the hunt binds identity to lasting harmony with the land. Cairne sends young hunters to track Arra'chea, a massive, solitary kodo bull roaming the grasslands below. Taking the bull's horn shows mastery of tracking prey across vast distances.

Bringing Arra'chea's horn to Thunder Bluff does more than display strength; it helps sustain the community. Tauren use every part of a slain beast. The trophy tells the High Chieftain where Arra'chea fell, so gathering parties can go down into the plains and harvest the kodo's thick hide and rich meat for the fledgling capital.
